zh.title: 空中巴士第二季獲利暴增126% 交付強勁帶動上半年營收成長12%
zh.summary: 空中巴士公布2026年上半年財報，第二季淨利年增126%至16.6億美元，營收年增28%。4至6月交付237架商用飛機，上半年合計交付351架。全年交付約870架的目標維持不變。
body: 空中巴士（Airbus）於2026年7月29日公布上半年財報，第二季強勁的商用飛機交付表現帶動獲利大幅成長。根據執行長Guillaume Faury說法，截至6月30日的三個月內，獲利較去年同期暴增126%。
數據顯示，空中巴士第二季淨利從去年同期的8.42億美元（7.32億歐元）攀升至16.6億美元（16.5億歐元），同期營收增加28%。上半年淨利則年增47%，來到25.8億美元（22.43億歐元）；上半年營收成長12%，達382億美元（332億歐元）。
交付量方面，空中巴士在2026年4月至6月間向客戶交付237架商用飛機，遠高於第一季的114架，使上半年總交付數達到351架。該公司重申全年交付約870架商用飛機的目標維持不變。
Faury表示，上半年的良好業績主要反映商用飛機交付量提升，以及國防與太空部門的強勁表現，儘管外部環境複雜且快速變遷。他強調，公司正全面加速以滿足對民用與軍用解決方案不斷增長的需求。
截至2026年6月底，空中巴士商用飛機累積訂單總額為886架，高於去年同期的494架，訂單儲備達9,222架。在產能規劃上，A220機型持續朝2028年月產13架的目標推進；A320系列則預計在2027年底前達到月產70至75架，之後穩定在月產75架。
空中巴士國防與太空部門上半年營收年增9%至72億美元（63億歐元），空中巴士直升機部門營收則大致持平，約為42億美元（36.8億歐元）。

en.title: Airbus profits surge 126% in Q2 on strong commercial deliveries, first-half revenue up 12%
en.summary: Airbus reported a 126% jump in second-quarter net income to $1.66 billion, driven by 237 commercial aircraft deliveries between April and June. First-half deliveries reached 351 units, revenue rose 12% to $38.2 billion, and the full-year target of around 870 deliveries was reaffirmed.
body: Airbus published its half-year 2026 results on July 29, with the second-quarter financial figures standing out. Net income surged 126% year-on-year to $1.66 billion in the three months to June 30, 2026, while revenue rose 28% over the same period, according to CEO Guillaume Faury.

For the first half of 2026, net income rose 47% to $2.58 billion, and revenues increased 12% to $38.2 billion from $34 billion a year earlier. The company attributed the improvement primarily to a higher level of commercial aircraft deliveries and strong performance in Defense and Space.

Between April and June 2026, Airbus delivered 237 commercial aircraft to customers, a sharp increase from the 114 delivered in the first quarter, bringing the first-half total to 351. The company said its ambition to deliver around 870 commercial aircraft in 2026 remains unchanged.

“Our good H1 results mainly reflect the higher level of commercial aircraft deliveries and strong performance in Defense and Space, against the backdrop of a complex and fast-changing environment,” Faury said. “We are ramping up across all businesses to meet the growing demand for our civil and military solutions.”

Gross commercial aircraft orders totalled 886 in the first six months of 2026, compared to 494 in the same period last year, and the order backlog stood at 9,222 aircraft at the end of June. Airbus continues to target a monthly A220 production rate of 13 in 2028, and a rate of 70 to 75 per month for the A320 family by end-2027, stabilising at rate 75 thereafter.
Revenues at Airbus Defense and Space increased 9% year-on-year to $7.2 billion, while Airbus Helicopters' revenues remained around $4.2 billion.
